originality.rationale: Against relevant same-observable full text, the known arbitrary-graph stabilizer sum and known GHZ/star expression do not imply the proved strict ordering without the new nontrivial inequality; checked biclique distribution literature uses a different noise process. Targeted searches and recoverable prior claims found no equivalent all-size hierarchy. Residual risk of unindexed or implicit enumerator literature remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier stabilizer weight-enumerator inequality for K_{a,b} may imply the same strict ordering.

The previously known general fidelity identity is strong computational coverage; novelty rests on the uniform strict hierarchy and asymptotic relative performance, not the general method or the star value.
The model is deliberately restricted to post-preparation IID depolarization, so conclusions cannot be imported into noisy preparation/gate protocols.

value.rationale: Graph-state fidelity is a standard experimentally pertinent diagnostic under depolarization, and source work explicitly motivates connectivity-dependent resilience. Within a physically meaningful two-class all-to-all architecture, the result makes an exact global selection: all intermediate configurations are strictly ordered for all interior noise strengths, and star fidelity asymptotically doubles balanced fidelity. It does not claim the computational stabilizer identity, known clique formula, or an entanglement threshold as new.
